observations.text: Let us plan the garden bench dimensions first.
We can compare a narrow and a wide seat.
One more topic: in ChatADHD, save an interrupted model response before changing providers.
For Loom SDK, keep a durable task checkpoint.
Now switch to dinner: the oven timer is unreliable.
Returning to the SDK task: it must resume from that checkpoint, not from the oven timer.
I am comparing our conversation app and a separate lighting console.
Both have a buffer.
It must survive restart.
Make that persistent.
A knitting counter and our ChatADHD client both keep history.
The counter can reset.
By it in the next sentence I mean the client: it must retain every edited turn.
First topic: my wooden loom makes woven cloth.
New topic: our Loom SDK must expose the C++ task callback.
At the fair I saw a loom and admired the woven cloth.
New topic: explain what a C++ SDK is in general.
Our client saves a response buffer.
The laboratory sensor also saves a response buffer.
New topic: it should use the smaller buffer.
We began by discussing a wooden loom and its cloth.
Later I started a separate Loom SDK task about C++ callbacks.
Back to the wooden loom: it needs a stronger frame.

interpretation: Actual source turns and entity aliases were inputs; labels and source expectations were withheld.
Local focus and segmentation are measured independently of whole-conversation project membership.
Overlapping observations with extra focus are counted as errors even if another span correctly names the entity.
This is an eight-conversation synthetic diagnostic, not general reference-resolution accuracy.
